A cross-sectional design was used to assess drug resistance among adult PLHIV with virologic nonsuppression in Malawi between July 2022 and February 2023. Abstract:  In Malawi, 95.6% of adult people living with HIV (PLHIV) on antiretroviral therapy (ART) use dolutegravir-based regimens (DBR), however, prevalence of dolutegravir resistance is unknown. We conducted a national HIV drug resistance (HIVDR) survey in adults on DBR with high viral load (VL) results after intensive adherence counseling (IAC).  

Among 213 participants with confirmed virologic failure, 212 samples were successfully genotyped for protease, reverse transcriptase, and integrase. Prevalence of drug resistance mutations (DRMs) to nucleotide reverse-transcriptase inhibitors was 22.6% (95% CI: 17.4% to 27.8%), to non-nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitors 55.1% (95% CI 48.2% to 62.1%), and to protease inhibitors 4.9% (95% CI 1.3% to 8.5%). Prevalence of major dolutegravir DRMs was 8.5% (95% CI 5.3% to 11.9%). DTG DRMs identified included G118R (8), E138K (8), R263K/A (5), Q148R (3), and T66A/I/V (3).
